text: Start with the inclusive integer range [26, 965]. First, keep only the numbers whose digits sum to 8. Then, retain only the odd integers. Then, scale every remaining value by a factor of 5. Next, replace each remaining number x with x * x. Next, replace each remaining number with the sum of its decimal digits (ignoring any minus sign). Of these numbers, give the mode of the remaining numbers, choosing the smallest value in case of a tie.

Take all integers between 359 and 910, including both endpoints. First, keep only the prime numbers. Then, keep only the numbers whose decimal digits add up to 16. Then, take every remaining value modulo 13, using the non-negative remainder (0 to 12). Next, replace every remaining value x with the digits of |x| written in reverse order, with the original sign restored and leading zeros dropped. Then, multiply each remaining number by 3. Of these numbers, find the greatest value among the remaining numbers.

Take all integers between 296 and 900, including both endpoints. First, keep only the numbers that are divisible by 5. Next, retain only the values below 662 (not including 662 itself). Next, retain only the values with a digit sum of exactly 6. Then, replace each remaining number by reversing the digits of its absolute value, keeping the original sign and dropping any leading zeros. Then, map every remaining value to the digit sum of its absolute value. Of these numbers, report how many numbers are left.

Start with the inclusive integer range [67, 584]. First, retain only the values above 226 (not including 226 itself). Then, discard every multiple of 10. Then, discard every number that is not prime. Next, retain only the values whose decimal representation includes the digit 2. Next, replace each remaining number x with 5 * x. Finally, compute the bitwise OR of all remaining values.

Consider the integers from 205 to 903, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 391 or greater. Next, keep only the numbers that are divisible by 6. Then, keep only the numbers whose digits sum to 15. Then, replace each remaining number x with x - 1. Next, replace each remaining number x with 2 * x. Of these numbers, give the number of zeros among the remaining values.

Take all integers between 52 and 568, including both endpoints. First, retain only the values that are not multiples of 7. Next, discard every number that does not have a 8 among its digits. Then, replace each remaining number x with the sum of the digits of |x|. Then, replace each remaining number x with x mod 13, where the result lies in 0 to 12. Then, replace each remaining number x with 2 * x. Finally, report the average of the remaining numbers rounded to an integer, rounding halves to the even neighbour.

Start with the inclusive integer range [71, 655]. First, keep only the prime numbers. Then, retain only the values above 432 (not including 432 itself). Next, replace each remaining number by reversing the digits of its absolute value, keeping the original sign and dropping any leading zeros. Take all integers between 105 and 348, including both endpoints. First, retain only the even integers. Then, retain only the values that are not multiples of 11. Next, replace every remaining value x with the digits of |x| written in reverse order, with the original sign restored and leading zeros dropped. Next, reverse the decimal digits of each remaining number (reverse the digits of its absolute value, keep the original sign, and drop any leading zeros). Next, replace each remaining number by reversing the digits of its absolute value, keeping the original sign and dropping any leading zeros. Consider the integers from 23 to 988, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers that are even. Then, keep only the numbers whose decimal digits add up to 12. Then, replace each remaining number with its remainder modulo 15, taken in the range 0 to 14. Of these numbers, count how many of the remaining values are equal to zero.

Consider the integers from 470 to 1000, inclusive. First, retain only the even integers. Then, keep only the numbers that are not divisible by 8. Start with the inclusive integer range [52, 995]. First, keep only the numbers that are even. Then, keep only the numbers that are divisible by 9. Consider the integers from 33 to 269, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers that are even. Next, keep only the numbers whose digits sum to 5. Then, decrease every remaining value by 2. Start with the inclusive integer range [143, 519]. First, discard every number that is 234 or smaller. Next, keep only the numbers whose decimal digits add up to 11. Consider the integers from 227 to 893, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers that contain the digit 6. Then, retain only the values above 569 (not including 569 itself). Next, retain only the primes. Next, replace each remaining number x with the sum of the digits of |x|. Then, replace each remaining number x with 2 * x. Of these numbers, report the minimum of the remaining values.

Consider the integers from 212 to 578, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers whose digits sum to 11. Then, discard every even number, keeping the odd ones. Next, reverse the decimal digits of each remaining number (reverse the digits of its absolute value, keep the original sign, and drop any leading zeros). Finally, compute the median of the remaining values (if the count is even, use the lower of the two middle values).

Then, scale every remaining value by a factor of 5. Then, replace each remaining number x with x + 9.
